label: Every first mover moved by none is…, from Over a supplied clock: at any time at which… and 1 more
meaning: Transcription (single application): the proof applies the lect. 8 reading, whose consequent is the conclusion's, after the bridge supplies its antecedent, so under invariant 16 it does not expand STMT-FIRST-UNMOVED-MOVER-IS-PURE-ACT on any route; the ST I q.3 a.1 derivation stays the selected proof. In Metaph. IX, lect. 8 n. 11 for the stage-1 pure-act statement, split from the one-time case statement (owner option B on #352). Premises: over a supplied clock, a mover moved in no respect at any time is, at any time at which it moves something, in potency in no respect (STMT-MOVER-MOVED-AT-NO-TIME-IS-PURE-ACT, the reading of 'primum movens, quod est in actu tantum'); and a first mover moved by none at a time is moved at no time (STMT-SLICE-FIRST-MOVER-MOVED-AT-NO-TIME, an open bridge that no claim states). Conclusion: at any time t, every first mover moved by none at t is pure act at t, which is STMT-FIRST-UNMOVED-MOVER-IS-PURE-ACT with the time-free prima via predicates instantiated at t (DEF-MOTION-AS-REDUCTION reads them at one time). Step: a first mover at t moves something at t, and by the bridge it is moved at no time, so the reading applies at t. Each premise is needed (primumMovensFacts): in the strictly forward feedback model of FIRST-WAY-SLICE-CONTROLS no mover is moved at no time, so the reading holds while the conclusion fails at t = 1; with one being, one respect and one time, a never-moved mover in potency satisfies the bridge and falsifies the conclusion. Both premises hold together in a model with a first mover at a time. Not used: act's simple priority, non-simultaneity, the first-being bridge, uniqueness. It closes nothing: the reading is a stated commitment without an argument for 'tantum', and the bridge is open and false in the feedback model.
